visualReview.notes: Inspected all11 current portable/source-terrain frames. Individual Thessaloniki Hagia Sophia with ochre upper west facade, three wood entries, four lower round window fields and ten narrow upper clerestory windows. The central portal has broad stepped round limestone arch bands. Warm masonry side/east walls, large polygonal central apse, two lower side apses and low tiered tile roofs follow the retained plans. The square brick drum has three large arched window fields per face, a short round crown and low gray-green ribbed metal dome/cross. The small northwest bell has a tiled hip cap and genuinely open paired upper arches. Removed a generated side window occluded by the bell, restricted ochre painting to the west wall and widened the central portal surround. Degenerate Float32 clipping remnants are omitted; no visible feature is removed by that filter. Exact carved reliefs/icons, tiny grille detail, inscriptions and interiors are omitted.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected all11 current shared-material/geographic frames. Replaced the first Flemish-brick binding, which read as vertical bands on the large walls, with the existing plain brick graph; the shared library itself is unchanged. Ochre plaster, warm masonry, muted tile, gray-green metal and pale stone use linear tints and metric UVs. Dark glass/grilles and gold accents use flat PBR colors. No embedded images, bespoke facade textures or baked weathering/shadows. Every graph reads once; unload disposes model geometry, leaves zero live model geometries and restores ground. Flat placement confirms plan alignment and partially hides below-datum entry geometry; source terrain views show the approximate entries/steps. Ground colors are diagnostic.
